subject: Post-call: Orbital.AI dedicated capacity needs, isolation & timeline
body:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Gordon <sam.gordon@orbital.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Orbital.AI dedicated capacity needs, isolation & timeline

Sam — great to meet you and the data team today. Thanks for walking us through the workload. Below is a short recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please flag anything missing or inaccurate.

Summary of pain / goals (as discussed)
- Predictable unit cost for real-time scoring during spikes: weekly peaks up to ~6k QPS for short windows (1–2 hours) and sustained baseline ~800–1,200 QPS.
- Strict tenant isolation: models ingesting PHI must run in an isolated dedicated pool (separate tenant / network) with separate NVMe cache lifecycle.
- Cold-start sensitivity: your serving pattern is bursty by user session; you need low tail latency (<150ms p95) and consistent p50 latency targets.
- Audit & compliance needs: retention windows, request-level audit logs, and KMS integration for key rotation.

Redwood recommended starting point (high level)
- Dedicated reserved pool: 4–8 GPUs (H100 equivalence) with reservation for predictable throughput + burst policy to scale to 12 GPUs for 2–4 hour windows.
- Isolation mode: private tenant with VPC peering and encrypted volumes; separate KV cache per tenant.
- SLAs: propose 99.95% uptime for dedicated pool and p95 latency goal configurable per route (we can scope per-model SLOs in the SOW).
- Onboarding: 2-week scoped PoC (functional, perf validation at your peak QPS, and failover tests), followed by 30-day ramp to steady state.

Data / technical assumptions we used in sizing
- Model family: 13B/16B dense + 2x smaller reranker models.
- Typical input length: 256 tokens; average response 120 tokens.
- KV cache hit expected: ~30% after warmup.
- Burst concurrency profile: concurrent connections up to ~2.5k during peaks.

Attached: preliminary quote, draft SOW, SLA table. These are intentionally conservative — we can tune after performance tests.

Immediate next steps
1) Monica to share formal SOW + quote (attached) and proposed billing cadence.
2) Your team to confirm which models will be in-scope for the PoC and any regulatory docs we should review (e.g., DPA, encryption attestations).
3) Schedule a 60-minute PoC kickoff next week (Avery will propose windows).

Owner / ETA
- Redwood: Monica Patel — SOW + scoped pricing (EOD Fri, 2027-04-02).
- Orbital: Sam — confirm model list and procurement path by Tue 2027-04-06.

Thanks again — we look forward to getting you to a deterministic cost model while keeping the isolation guarantees in place.

Best,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

--
Attachments: orbital-dedicated-quote.pdf (pdf), SOW-Orbital-Redwood-v1.docx (docx), SLA-table.xlsx (xlsx)


On Thu, 1 Apr 2027 at 12:04 PM, Sam Gordon <sam.gordon@orbital.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Karthik — this looks right from our side. Quick clarifications:
>
> - Procurement lead here is procurement@orbital.ai; they typically need a line-item quote + SOW for legal review.
> - Lead time concern: hardware commitments we were worried about — would Redwood provide a burst window (we liked the 12 GPU recommendation) but also a guaranteed baseline for sustained traffic? We need clear fallbacks if burst capacity is constrained.
> - Support hours: we operate 24/7; can you confirm escalation hours and whether on-call overlap is included in the reserved plan?
>
> Proposed time for the PoC kickoff: Tue 2027-04-06 11:00am PT. That works for our infra and data team.
>
> I'll loop procurement on the next email.
>
> —Sam
> VP of Engineering | Orbital.AI
> sam.gordon@orbital.ai | +1 (212) 555-0199
>
>
> On Thu, 1 Apr 2027 at 14:30, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Hi Sam / procurement@orbital.ai —
> >
> > Appreciate the quick responses. Attaching: formal SOW (scope + milestones), itemized pricing (line items for reserved GPUs, burst capacity, SLA credits), and a suggested monthly billing cadence.
> >
> > A few procurement notes:
> > - We can offer net-30 billing for committed pools; for customers requesting hardware-specific SKU reservation we may require a signed commitment term (6–12 months).
> > - SLA credits are defined in the SLA-table.xlsx. We usually include a 24x7 escalation channel for Dedicated customers in the Enterprise tier; that includes one named on-call engineer during the first 90 days of onboarding.
> > - If Orbital needs a stricter isolation guarantee (physically separated nodes or dedicated host pools), we can scope that as an addendum — that will change unit costs and lead time.
> >
> > Monica Patel
> > Senior Customer Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
> > monica_patel@redwood.com
> >
> > --
> > Attachments: SOW-Orbital-Redwood-v1.docx, SLA-table.xlsx

All good here. Procurement looped in and they asked for: a) final SOW with signatures, b) NET-30 PO entry, and c) a DocuSign link for the SOW. I pasted a placeholder DocuSign link below for your legal team to use in the SOW we received earlier.

Also confirming PoC kickoff Tue 2027-04-06 11:00am PT (Avery — if you can lock a calendar invite that would be great).

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

—Sam
